jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Company Overview:

Strive Pharmacy is a personalized compounding pharmacy built on a simple conviction: medicine should fit the patient, not the other way around. We started Strive because we believed the pharmaceutical industry was overdue for a more human approach—one that prioritizes individualized care, clinical nuance, and genuine partnership with patients and providers.

Compounding gives us the tools to do that. Every formulation we prepare is built to the specific needs of a specific person, and every interaction we have is guided by that same commitment to personalized care.

We're growing, and we're looking for people who share that conviction. If you're ready to be part of a pharmacy that takes the work seriously and the people even more seriously, we'd like to meet you.

Mission:

Strive exists to disrupt an industry long overdue for a more personal approach to care. We put the human element at the center of everything: every formulation, every patient interaction, every provider partnership. We're not just a compounding pharmacy. We're a team on a mission to change what personalized healthcare looks and feels like.

Location
: Remote (MST hours), Onsite in Mesa, AZ a plus

Position Type:
Full-Time

Schedule:
M-F 8-5, Arizona time zone

Salary:
$100,000 - $115,000

Position Overview:

As a Project Manager at Strive you will be instrumental in shaping and executing various company strategies. In this role, you will be responsible for leading and managing projects primarily focused on site operations initiatives, while also contributing to projects across various departments. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to ensure that all efforts align with our company’s goals and objectives.

Key Responsibilities:

Lead the planning, execution, and delivery of projects, ensuring they are completed on time, within scope, and on budget.
Assist with department specific workload & resource management, aligning with department management on project roadmap planning and execution.
Coordinate internal resources and third parties/vendors for the flawless execution of projects.
Develop detailed project plans to track progress and adapt to scope adjustments.
Manage the relationship with all stakeholders, ensuring effective communication throughout the project lifecycle.
Perform risk management to minimize project risks.
Create and maintain comprehensive project documentation.
Measure project performance using appropriate systems, tools, and techniques.
Report and escalate to management as needed.
Manage the project budget, including invoicing and ensuring financial accuracy.
Coordinate resources to support project execution and achieve desired outcomes.
Drive process improvements and optimization initiatives within the PMO and across the organization, leveraging lessons learned and best practices.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Business, healthcare, or related field.
Proven working experience (5+ years) as a project manager in a related field.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong understanding of agile project management methodologies, such as Scrum or Kanban, and experience applying them in a professional setting.
Solid organizational skills, including multitasking and time-management.
Ability to lead and inspire a team.
Strong communication skills.
Proficiency in project management software tools.

Bonus Qualifications:

PMP / Scrum Master certification is a plus.
Creative problem-solving skills.
High attention to detail.
Assertive and able to lead team meetings.
Experience using Asana.

Work
Environment:

This position operates in a remote work environment. The role requires regular sitting, keyboarding, computer use, and virtual meetings. Occasional travel may be required.

Annual Salary: $100,000 USD - $115,000 USD

Join Us in Making an Impact:

At Strive, the work is real and the impact is direct. Every role here contributes to a patient experience that's more personal, more attentive, and more human than what most people have come to expect from a pharmacy. Apply today and help us raise the bar.

Benefits/ Perks:

Strive Pharmacy offers a comprehensive benefits package, including:

Employer-paid healthcare coverage, effective the 1st day of the following month of your hire date
Free Strive compounded medications for employees based on a valid patient-specific prescription from a licensed healthcare provider
Paid time off
Sick time
FSA and HSA options
Parental leave
401(k) with employer matching
Life insurance

Culture:

Culture isn't an afterthought at Strive. It's something we actively build. We foster a collaborative, engaging workplace where employees have opportunities to connect, celebrate, and build meaningful relationships with their colleagues. We're committed to supporting the personal and professional growth of every employee, both inside and outside the workplace.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Product
jobs.description:
Form Health is a virtual obesity medicine clinic delivering multi-disciplinary evidence-based obesity treatment through telemedicine. Obesity impacts more than 40% of the US adult population, and although historically only about 1% of patients received medical treatment for their disease, the field of Obesity Medicine is entering a period of rapid growth. Form Health provides high-quality expert care and leverages technology to enhance the patient experience. All Form Health patients work closely with their care team, which includes board certified physicians, advanced practice professionals and Registered Dietitians. Through our proprietary mobile app patients engage in regular video visits, as well as text messaging, photo journaling, digital data transmission, and customized educational materials. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of clinical care, and to treating every individual with empathy and respect.

Founded in 2019, Form Health is a venture-backed innovative startup with an experienced clinical and leadership team. Our mission is to empower patients and be leaders in Obesity Medicine driving impact at a national scale. We are deeply invested in our core value to put patients first, and also deeply committed to creating a culture where every employee is valued and we learn and improve together.

Form Health is a virtual obesity medicine clinic delivering physician-led, evidence-based care for obesity and related cardiometabolic conditions. Obesity affects more than 40% of U.S. adults, and as GLP-1 medications reshape the field, Obesity and Cardiometabolic Medicine is in a period of rapid growth and opportunity. Form Health is at the forefront of that shift, building a clinical model that combines rigorous, personalized medical care with the technology to make it accessible at scale.

Every Form Health patient works closely with a dedicated multidisciplinary Care Team, including board-certified physicians (many ABOM-certified, and endocrinologists), advanced practice providers, and Registered Dietitians who together deliver comprehensive, one-on-one treatment that includes nutrition, behavioral health, physical activity, and FDA-approved medication, if appropriate. Through our mobile app, patients engage in regular video visits along with text messaging, photo journaling, and personalized educational content. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of clinical care and to treating every individual with empathy and respect.

Founded in 2019, Form Health is a venture-backed, mission-driven company partnering with leading employers and health plans to expand access to high-quality, guideline-based obesity and cardiometabolic care nationwide. We're deeply invested in our core value of putting patients first, and equally committed to building a culture where every employee is valued and we learn and grow together.

About The Role

The Senior Program Manager, Product is a critical, highly independent role at the center of Form Health's Product organization. You'll be the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, Clinical, and go-to-market teams — and the person responsible for making sure our Product org operates as a best-in-class, AI-forward, product development team.

This is a builder's role, not a caretaker's. You'll define the Product Operations roadmap from the ground up, bring in and champion cutting-edge tools and methodologies (including AI-assisted planning, development, and research workflows), and continuously raise the bar on how the team plans, ships, and learns. You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy — setting priorities, making judgment calls, and driving initiatives to completion with minimal oversight — while staying closely aligned with Product, Engineering, and executive stakeholders.

What You Will Do

Own the Product Operations roadmap: Independently define the vision, priorities, and success metrics for how the Product org plans, builds, ships, and learns — identifying gaps and driving initiatives from idea to adoption.
Drive end-to-end program management: Own execution roadmaps for key cross-functional initiatives — from new clinical program features to platform investments — ensuring timely, high-quality delivery from concept to launch.
Orchestrate cross-functional alignment: Serve as the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, Design, Clinical Operations, Marketing, and Customer Success — facilitating the rituals, decisions, and communication that keep every team moving in the same direction.
Champion AI-forward tools and methodologies: Evaluate, pilot, and roll out modern product development tooling — AI-assisted planning, coding, research, and automation — to help the team plan and ship faster. Treat AI as core infrastructure for how the team works, not a side project.
Build and evolve the product operating model: Design and continuously improve how the team runs, including intake and triage processes, roadmap and sprint rituals, documentation standards, and tooling that scale with the company.
Turn data and feedback into decisions: Synthesize product usage data, clinical and operational metrics, and patient/customer feedback into clear, actionable recommendations that inform roadmap and prioritization.
Provide executive visibility: Develop and deliver program health readouts and roadmap updates to leadership, with data-driven insights, risks, and recommendations.
Proactively manage risk and dependencies: Identify, assess, and mitigate issues that could impact timelines or quality across teams, escalating and resolving blockers before they become critical.
Interface directly with stakeholders: Act as a trusted partner and clear point of contact for Product-related questions from Clinical, Commercial, Ops, and executive leadership.

About You

5+ years of progressive experience in program/project management, product operations, or a related discipline within a fast-paced software or digital health environment.
A demonstrated track record of operating highly independently — you've built a roadmap, process, or operating model from scratch, not just executed against someone else's plan.
Fluency with modern product development tools and genuine enthusiasm for AI-forward workflows (e.g., AI-assisted planning, coding, and research tools, alongside Linear, Figma, etc.).
Deep understanding of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) and Agile methodologies, with the judgment to adapt them to what a team actually needs rather than applying them rigidly.
Strong analytical skills — comfortable pulling and interpreting product, engineering, and operational data to inform decisions.
Outstanding cross-functional communication and influence — able to distill ambiguous, complex problems into clear plans and align stakeholders, from ICs to executives, without relying on direct authority.
Experience in digital health, healthcare operations, or another regulated/clinical environment is a strong plus.
Bachelor's degree in a technical, business, or related field preferred; PMP, PgMP, or similar certification a plus.

More About Form Health’s Benefits

Competitive salary and equity in a high growth start-up
Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)
401k program
Flexible work schedules and paid time off
Paid parental leave

The Opportunity

As Project Manager
, you will play a pivotal leadership role
in driving the Galore Creek project toward its ultimate development decision. Initially reporting directly to the Director, Project Services
, you will unite and lead a cross-functional delivery team, seamlessly integrating Technical, Engineering, and SERA (Social, Environmental, and Regulatory Affairs) scopes from the initial engineering stages straight through to construction. 

Key Accountabilities

Integrated Scopes:
Drive technical, economic, risk, and regulatory outcomes that justify sound investment decisions and advance the project lifecycle.
Stage & Execution Planning:
Support the strategic planning and organization of the Project's next phases.
Third-party Vendor Management:
Oversee and manage external service providers to ensure high-quality delivery.
Stage Deliverable Review:
Collaborate with internal teams to review, refine, and formally endorse project deliverables.

Work Environment and Travel

While this is an office-based role
, it requires occasional travel across Northern BC
. This includes spending time on-site at the Galore Creek Project
and engaging directly within the communities of our Indigenous partners
and Communities of Interest (COIs).

About Us

Located in Tahltan Territory in Northwestern British Columbia, Galore Creek is one of the world’s largest undeveloped copper-gold-silver deposits. Galore Creek Mining Corporation (GCMC) is a 50:50 partnership between Newmont Corporation (Newmont) and Teck Resources Limited (Teck), committed to advancing the asset towards a development decision with meaningful input and support from the Tahltan Nation and B.C. regulators. GCMC has a long-standing relationship with the Tahltan Nation and local communities, including collaboration during regulatory processes, reviews of environmental performance, and preferential contracting and employment opportunities. 

As a GCMC employee, you will join an inclusive, results-driven team guided by our core values. Together, you will help responsibly advance a world-class copper-gold mine, creating long-term value through the sustainable production of critical minerals. Learn more about Galore Creek at www.gcmc.ca. 

Responsibilities

Ensure GCMC’s commitment to excellence by recognizing our core values
of health and safety, people, responsible development, continuous improvement and innovation, and integrity.
Lead the integration of Technical, Engineering, and SERA scopes
, working with each function to align deliverables, schedules, and interfaces, so the Project moves forward as one team.
Work with internal teams and external consultants
to ensure SERA requirements, including commitments to environmental, permitting, community, Indigenous partners, and COIs into Technical and Engineering design and planning at appropriate stages.
Lead preparation of project plans, technical decisions, status reporting, and technical briefings
for GCMC senior leadership and the Teck and Newmont governance Committees (i.e. Technical, SERA, and Finance Committees).
Provide
guidance and technical direction in the development of design and construction standards in the project, as well as maintaining the design and construction standards.
Coordinate
and manage the work efforts of numerous contractors, specialist contractors, and consultants.
Contribute to planning, design, budgeting, and contracting strategy
, including resource plans, investment-stage objectives, and critical success factors, in close collaboration with the Project Team.
Build strong, trusting relationships
with project team members and external partners (e.g., owners, contractors, and COIs).
Support and empower the team to achieve its goals
and contribute to a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and value creation.
Lead scope-appropriate risk management
, working with the team to identify technical, commercial, and schedule risks across the study and development lifecycle and develop mitigation strategies.
Develop fit-for-purpose systems, processes, and procedures
while promoting innovation, creative thinking where and when it benefits the Project.
Implement and maintain quality control procedures
so integrated Project deliverables meet the required standards.

The above responsibilities are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and are not necessarily all-inclusive.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Mining, or a related field
. Possessing an MBA is an asset. PMP and/or P.Eng. is preferred
.
12+ years of progressive experience
in mining technical studies or project development, with a track record of leading multidisciplinary study programs. Experience delivering studies on base metals, critical minerals, or other major mining development projects is preferred.
Experience delivering projects in remote and complex mountainous terrain
, ideally in NW British Columbia or the Yukon.
Proven collaborative leadership
, with the ability to guide and support employees, consultants, and multidisciplinary teams, balance competing priorities, and deliver high-quality work.
Seasoned understanding of project management fundamentals
, including project controls, scheduling, scope, risk, and interface management.
Exceptional communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills
, with the ability to convey complex technical information for audiences ranging from communities to executives.
Strong business and strategic judgement
, with the ability to understand project and business drivers, identify effective solutions, influence decisions, and build alignment.
A genuine team player with a track record of effectively collaborating
across technical, engineering, environmental, regulatory, community, and executive functions.
Proven ability to build and maintain positive, trusting relationships with Indigenous Peoples and Communities of Interest
, with a clear understanding of social and Project risk.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills
.
Ability to work in remote terrain, uneven surfaces, and all-weather conditions.
Satisfactory Criminal Record and Background Checks. 
Valid Class 5 Driver’s Licence. 
Legally authorized to work in Canada. 

What to Expect

A dynamic hybrid work arrangement (3 days in-office / 2 days remote), with occasional travel throughout the broader Northern BC region, including the Galore Creek site and rural remote communities.
A collaborative, safety-focused workplace culture. 
Competitive compensation and benefits package.
Professional growth opportunities within a major development-stage mining project.

This could be the delivery of a complete software implementation to a client or the delivery of a new features. Project Managers own their projects; they do not directly manage personnel or personnel budgets but must identify the skills and resources required to complete the scope of their projects on schedule, including the management of project budgets. 

JANA’s Project Managers are responsible for guiding projects from conception to completion, ensuring projects are completed on time and within budget. Several projects are typically in the process of being completed at any given time, and a Project Manager must be able to manage multiple aspects of the process simultaneously. Project Managers work cross-functionally and communicate to all parties involved in a project.

Manages and coordinates multiple projects throughout the project lifecycle.  
Accountable for meeting budget, timelines, and resource commitments

Fast/Agile: Removes barriers to move faster, experiments and adapts, thrives under pressure and fast pace.

Job Summary

The Program Manager, interRAI Practice & Data Quality leads the development, implementation and oversight of a coordinated interRAI program across the organization. The role ensures the organization’s interRAI governance, policies, processes and reporting practices are consistent with Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) program criteria, standards and submission requirements.

The Program Manager leads initial training, competency development and assessment, ongoing practice support and a coordinated approach to maintain assessor competency. Working collaboratively with clinical practice, research, operations, quality, digital health and analytics teams, the role supports data quality and compliance audits and the integration of interRAI instruments into electronic clinical documentation and workflows.

The Program Manager supports the use of interRAI information at the clinical, program and organizational levels to strengthen care planning, identify population and performance trends, support quality improvement and inform organizational decision-making. The role requires a master’s-prepared regulated health professional with demonstrated interRAI program leadership expertise.

ACCOUNTABILITY

InterRAI Leadership and Governance:
Define, standardize, and govern enterprise and Lines of Business (LoB) level operational KPIs, ensuring clarity, comparability, and alignment to organizational goals.
Lead the development, implementation and oversight of an coordinated interRAI program across organizational settings and instruments.
Establish and maintain the program framework, governance, policies, standards and accountabilities needed to support consistent implementation.
Ensure program alignment with organizational priorities, clinical documentation and practice expectations and applicable CIHI program criteria and standards.
Identify program priorities, risks, and resource needs for consideration by accountable leaders.

Education, Competency and Program Enablement:
Establish organization-wide expectations for assessor preparation, competency, coding reliability and ongoing InterRAI practice support.
Lead the development and oversight of standardized education, competency assessment, tools and resources.
Ensure interRAI instruments are effectively integrated into clinical assessment, care planning workflows and documentation processes.
Collaborate with clinical practice, education and operational teams to support implementation, ongoing practice support and maintenance of competency.

Program Quality, Compliance and Data Integrity:
Establish and maintain a comprehensive quality and compliance audit framework addressing assessment completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, coding reliability and submission requirements.
Oversee monitoring, auditing and reporting processes to identify data quality, compliance and program implementation gaps.
Establish and oversee issue escalation, corrective action and continuous improvement processes in collaboration with accountable leaders.
Ensure interRAI practices and data submissions remain aligned with internal policies, jurisdictional requirements and applicable CIHI program criteria and standards.

Data Utilization, Performance Improvement and Decision Support:
Enable effective use of interRAI information to support clinical care, quality improvement, program planning and organizational decision-making.
Collaborate with clinical practice, quality, operations, digital health and analytics teams to define priority reporting and data use requirements.
Promote use of interRAI data to understand client and population needs and support clinical practice, program improvement, evaluation and organizational planning.
Define requirements for the integration of interRAI information into electronic documentation systems
Enable the use of interRAI data to inform quality improvement initiatives, performance monitoring and strategic planning.

Qualifications

Master’s Degree in nursing, health administration, health informatics, health sciences, quality improvement, leadership or a related field
Minimum four years of relevant experience leading or coordinating a multi-site, multi-program or organization-wide interRAI, clinical, quality, health information or professional practice program.

Additional Skills / Core Capabilities

Current registration in good standing with a provincial or territorial health regulatory body.
Demonstrated experience developing, implementing or overseeing a coordinated interRAI program within a healthcare organization. Preference will be given to candidates with expertise in interRAI Homecare and interRAI Long-Term Care Facilities.
Strong knowledge of the interRAI assessment system, and demonstrated expertise with the instruments used by the organization.
Successful completion of applicable education for the instruments within the scope of the role, or the ability to complete required education within a defined period following appointment.
Demonstrated ability to interpret and apply interRAI instrument manuals, coding standards, assessment conventions, reference materials, data-quality requirements and related clinical and organizational outputs.
Knowledge of CIHI requirements for the Integrated interRAI Reporting System (IRRS), including data standards, mandatory data elements, business rules, validation processes, submission requirements and reporting practices.
Demonstrated knowledge of the clinical and organizational application of interRAI outputs, including outcome scales, Collaborative Action Plans, quality indicators, case-mix groupings and other decision-support tools.
Experience establishing or overseeing interRAI education, assessor competency, coding reliability, inter-rater reliability, coaching and practice-support models.
Strong knowledge of interRAI data quality, including assessment completeness, coding accuracy, internal consistency, timeliness, reliability, validation and submission-error management.
Demonstrated ability to analyze, interpret and translate interRAI information into actionable clinical, program, quality, and organizational insights.
Experience using interRAI data to support care planning, risk identification, population-health analysis, benchmarking, quality improvement, resource planning and performance monitoring.
Experience developing or overseeing interRAI data quality and compliance audit processes.
Ability to identify data-quality risks and distinguish among clinical practice issues, coding or competency concerns, workflow problems and system or configuration errors.
Experience defining clinical documentation and workflow requirements in collaboration with digital health teams.
Experience collaborating with clinical practice, research, quality, operations, analytics, digital health and clinical informatics teams to establish reporting requirements and support accurate interpretation and use of interRAI data.
Experience in clinical practice transformation, quality improvement, organizational change and evidence-informed decision-making.
Strong research and analytical skills, including the ability to evaluate evidence, interpret complex data and integrate findings into clinical practice and organizational decision-making.
Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to engage regulated health professionals, educators, operational leaders, interdisciplinary teams, technical specialists and senior leadership.
Demonstrated ability to provide subject matter expertise, establish credibility and influence decision-making at all levels of the organization.
Demonstrated bility to challenge existing practices constructively and act as a catalyst for evidence-informed improvement and positive change.
Demonstrated ability to establish program expectations and support others to apply, teach, coach and reinforce interRAI standards and practices.
Knowledge of relevant regulatory, privacy, clinical documentation and health-information requirements across Canadian provinces and territories.
Strong organizational, planning and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple and often competing priorities across programs and jurisdictions.
Demonstrated critical-thinking, analytical, decision-making and problem-resolution skills.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and working knowledge of Word, Outlook and PowerPoint. Experience with business intelligence or data-visualization platforms is an asset.
Membership in a relevant professional association, such as the Registered Nurses’ Association of Ontario or Canadian Nurses Association, is preferred.
Additional certification in leadership, quality improvement, project management or change management, such as Lean Six Sigma, PMP or Prosci, is an asset.
Ability to travel periodically and access to a vehicle are required. Occasional after-hours availability may be required to support significant program, system or compliance matters

Appleton, Wisconsin
Employment Type:

About SMT Surface Mount Technology Corporation (SMT) is an Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) provider specializing in complex, custom electronics manufacturing.
Since 1997, SMT has supported customers with demanding manufacturing requirements, combining technical capability, responsive decision-making and a strong focus on execution.
We are looking for a Program Manager
to serve as the primary point of contact for assigned customers and coordinate successful execution across our manufacturing organization.

About the Position This is a hands-on, customer-facing manufacturing role.
Program Managers at SMT are responsible for understanding customer needs, coordinating internal resources, communicating clearly as conditions change and ensuring commitments are carried through.
Success requires more than providing status updates. It takes judgment, accountability, follow-through and the ability to bring Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Quality and Planning together around a common execution plan.

Key Responsibilities Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned customers and build strong, trusted relationships.
Understand customer requirements, priorities and changing business needs.
Coordinate execution across Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Planning and other departments.
Manage customer orders, purchase-order alignment, demand changes and execution flow.
Monitor production schedules and communicate status, risks and changes clearly and proactively.
Coordinate customer-requested changes, evaluate internal impacts and provide timely responses.
Support new-product introductions, production ramps and ongoing manufacturing programs.
Help resolve execution issues and escalate matters when appropriate.
Monitor program performance against expected sales and customer demand.
Identify opportunities to expand relationships with existing customers.
Maintain accurate follow-up and ensure customer commitments are understood and executed internally.
Help customers understand the information, approvals and decisions SMT needs to execute successfully.

Qualifications Strong candidates will typically demonstrate:
Experience in electronics manufacturing, EMS or another manufacturing environment.
Experience working directly with customers and managing professional relationships.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate difficult information clearly.
Ability to coordinate across multiple departments without relying on formal authority.
Sound judgment, practical problem-solving skills and the ability to perform under pressure.
Strong organization, accountability and follow-through.
Ability to manage competing customer priorities.
Familiarity with production schedules, customer orders, demand planning and manufacturing data.
Ability to recognize risks, manage issues and escalate appropriately.
A demonstrated commitment to customer satisfaction and execution.

A four-year degree is preferred, but relevant manufacturing experience and demonstrated capability are more important.

Previous EMS or electronics manufacturing experience is especially valuable, including familiarity with customer demand, material constraints, engineering changes, contract manufacturing and production execution.

Who May Be a Strong Fit Candidates may come from backgrounds including EMS Program Management, Customer Program Management, Manufacturing Account Management, Customer Service within manufacturing, Materials or Production Coordination, Supply Chain, or Operations roles with significant customer-facing responsibility.

What Makes SMT Different SMT is a smaller, flatter organization than many large EMS providers.
Our Program Managers work directly with the people responsible for manufacturing execution, including Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Operations and company leadership.
That provides meaningful visibility, responsibility and the opportunity to influence decisions.
We value clear communication, early identification of risks, accountability, practical problem-solving and long-term customer relationships.
Our philosophy is simple: Execution Over Talk.

SMT has been manufacturing electronics in Appleton since 1997 and has paid profit sharing for 10 consecutive years.

Work Environment This is a full-time, on-site position in Appleton, Wisconsin. Program Managers work closely with manufacturing teams and are expected to be actively engaged with customers and internal departments throughout the business day.

jobs.description:

to revolutionize energy efficiency in commercial buildings. Our autonomous software optimizes heating and cooling systems, reducing energy consumption by 20–30%
, without requiring new hardware.
We work with leading European real estate owners and asset managers, with our technology already deployed across around 100 buildings and over 2 million m²
. We operate across Europe, with entities in France, Germany and Poland
.
We're entering a new phase of growth, with ambitious plans to accelerate commercial expansion, scale our organization, and broaden our offering.
Our ambition is to make autonomous energy optimization the new standard across European commercial real estate.

The company Thermosphr is a fast-growing European climate-tech company using AI and advanced engineering
to revolutionize energy efficiency in commercial buildings. Our autonomous software optimizes heating and cooling systems, reducing energy consumption by 20–30%
, without requiring new hardware.
We work with leading European real estate owners and asset managers, with our technology already deployed across around 100 buildings and over 2 million m²
. We operate across Europe, with entities in France, Germany and Poland
.
We're entering a new phase of growth, with ambitious plans to accelerate commercial expansion, scale our organization, and broaden our offering.
Our ambition is to make autonomous energy optimization the new standard across European commercial real estate.

What you will do How do we manage 15x more buildings with just 2-3x more people?
That's the challenge our Operational Excellence team is here to solve.
Our ambition is simple: make every team at Thermosphr dramatically more productive, by combining the smartest people, processes, and technologies. We believe talented people should spend their time solving interesting problems, not drowning in repetitive, low-value tasks.
Your mission?
Get your hands dirty, challenge how things work, and build better ways of doing things across the company.
Make our operations scalable.
Rethink how we deploy buildings, manage information, coordinate teams, and deliver our services, so that growing 10x doesn't mean working 10x harder.
Eliminate low-value work.
Simplify workflows, cut unnecessary steps, and automate repetitive tasks. Make sure our people spend their talent where it really counts.
Turn ideas into results.
Take ownership of your initiatives, bring people on board with Operations, Product, Sales and other teams, and drive implementation until you get real results.
Build, test, iterate.
Experiment with AI, automation, no-code tools, and software integrations. Prototype solutions, put them into people's hands, learn what works, and keep improving.
Win people over.
Bring teams along from day one, support them through the change, and keep going until adoption is real and the gains are measurable.
Think cutting weeks off building deployments, building an AI-powered assistant for internal teams, or automating a workflow that currently eats up hours of someone's week.
No endless recommendations or PowerPoint strategies. We want people who make things happen.

We're looking for a sharp, curious, and resourceful individual with a strong drive to make things happen. Someone who sees a problem as an opportunity, loves figuring things out, and gets real satisfaction from making things work better.
You're a natural problem solver.
You think analytically, ask the right questions, challenge assumptions, and find smart, pragmatic solutions to complex problems.

You're a builder, not just a thinker.
You'd rather test an imperfect solution today than spend weeks designing the perfect one. You're not afraid to experiment, fail, learn, and try again.

You're relentlessly curious.
You love learning new things, quickly get your head around unfamiliar topics, and have a genuine interest in technology, AI, and automation.

You make people around you better.
You're a great listener and communicator, enjoy working closely with others, and know how to challenge, convince, and bring people on board without imposing your ideas.

You take ownership.
You're proactive, autonomous, and resourceful. You don't wait for someone to tell you what to do, and you don't consider a job done until it delivers results.

You have high standards, without taking yourself too seriously.

Project Manager - Metallurgical Complex

Reports to: Maintenance Manager

About the Opportunity

Our client is looking for a Project Manager to lead capital, maintenance, infrastructure, and improvement projects at a large metallurgical processing complex. You'll own projects from the first conversation about what the plant needs all the way through commissioning, handover, and closeout, and you'll do it while the plant keeps running.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who knows how processing plants actually work and can bring Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, and contractors together around one plan. You'll manage a portfolio of projects of different sizes, have a real say in what gets prioritized, and see the results of your work on the plant floor.

What You'll Do

Project Development and Governance

Work with Operations and Maintenance to define project needs, benefits, requirements, alternatives, and acceptance criteria
Develop or coordinate feasibility assessments, scopes of work, design criteria, cost estimates, economic analyses, schedules, procurement strategies, and AFE documentation
Set project baselines and governance, including decision rights, stage-gate reviews, change control, risk registers, reporting cadence, and escalation thresholds
Manage a portfolio of projects and recommend priorities based on safety, compliance, operational risk, value, and resource capacity

Engineering, Procurement, and Contractors

Coordinate multidisciplinary engineering and review drawings, specifications, calculations, estimates, and construction methods for code compliance, constructability, operability, and maintainability
Prepare bid packages, support contractor selection and negotiations, and manage contractor performance on safety, quality, schedule, cost, and documentation
Coordinate labor, materials, equipment, outages, access, permits, inspections, and testing with affected departments and outside parties

Execution, Controls, and Risk

Direct work from planning through construction and commissioning, resolving constraints and limiting disruption to plant operations
Track actual performance against scope, schedule, budget, forecast, and quality, analyze variances, keep commitments and accruals accurate, and put recovery plans in place
Identify risks, dependencies, and opportunities, assign owners, carry out mitigations, and escalate material changes for timely decisions
Apply QA/QC requirements, inspection and test plans, and acceptance protocols suited to the work

Safety, Environmental, and Regulatory

Lead projects in line with site safety standards, environmental requirements, permits, codes, and management-of-change protocols, and stop work when conditions are unsafe or noncompliant
Build hazard identification, constructability, operability, maintainability, and environmental controls into planning, design reviews, contractor mobilization, execution, and closeout
Make sure incidents, near misses, compliance concerns, and material risks are reported, investigated, escalated, and addressed on time

Team Leadership, Reporting, and Closeout

Lead cross-functional project teams, set clear expectations, facilitate decisions, and coach contributors
Build productive relationships with site leaders, employees, contractors, consultants, vendors, and agencies
Give sponsors and stakeholders concise, timely reporting on progress, forecast, milestones, risks, decisions, and outcomes
Complete commissioning and handover with Operations and Maintenance, including training, procedures, PM updates, spare parts, warranties, as-builts, asset records, financial closeout, and lessons learned

What You Bring

Education

Bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, project management, or a closely related field (substantial relevant experience may be considered in place of a degree)
Mechanical or Electrical Engineering degree preferred

Experience

7+ years of progressively responsible engineering, construction, maintenance, or capital project experience in mining, mineral processing, metals, heavy manufacturing, or a comparable industrial setting
Proven track record taking multidisciplinary projects through planning, design, budgeting, procurement, construction, commissioning, and closeout with minimal supervision
Experience leading teams of engineers, plant operators, maintenance staff, and contractors from project development through start-up
5+ years of project experience in an OSHA-regulated processing plant, smelter, refinery, foundry, or similar continuous facility preferred
Experience with process flow systems, structural modifications, reliability improvement, cost modeling, forecasting, and capital governance preferred

Certifications

PMP or comparable project management credential preferred
PE license or EIT certification preferred, where it applies to the discipline

Key Skills

Strong grasp of the full project lifecycle and of scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk, procurement, contract, change, and document controls
Working knowledge of industrial processing operations and maintenance, including how equipment, utilities, infrastructure, and production constraints interact
Capital budgeting, cost estimating, forecasting, accruals, economic evaluation, and asset capitalization
Knowledge of OSHA requirements, environmental compliance, permitting, engineering codes, and safe contractor management
General knowledge of collective bargaining agreements and how they affect project planning and execution
Ability to lead and influence across functions, resolve conflict, and make sound decisions as conditions change
Clear written, verbal, presentation, and negotiation skills for technical and nontechnical audiences
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, MS Project or equivalent, and AutoCAD, with the ability to read drawings and specifications
JD Edwards or equivalent CMMS experience preferred

Why Join

End-to-end ownership of projects, from defining the need through handover and closeout
A varied portfolio of capital, maintenance, infrastructure, and improvement work
A real voice in which projects get prioritized and how they're delivered
5-2-4-3 schedule with 9-hour days
A team culture built on innovation, commitment, accountability, respect, enabling others, and safety

What Success Looks Like

Projects meet their approved safety, environmental, quality, scope, schedule, and cost commitments, with timely recovery plans for any material variances
Forecasts, commitments, accruals, risk registers, schedules, and status reports are current, accurate, and on time
Stage-gate, AFE, procurement, permitting, management-of-change, and document control steps are complete before work moves forward
Contractors meet site expectations for safety, quality, productivity, schedule, cost, and closeout documentation
Commissioning, handover, asset records, and financial closeout are finished with documented stakeholder sign-off
Completed projects deliver their intended operational, reliability, compliance, or financial results, with lessons learned captured

A Note on Fit

We understand no candidate will meet every single desired qualification. If your experience looks a little different from what we've identified and you think you can bring value to the role, we'd love to learn more about you!

Project Manager

7 Months

Phoenix, AZ 85007 Hybrid

The candidates will need to go into the office as needed

Must be local to Phoenix

Project Manager PD

1. Job Summary

Reporting directly to the Strategy Manager for the Division of Aging and Adult Services (DAAS), the Project Manager leads high-impact strategic initiatives, continuous improvement projects, and large-scale operational transformations across the division. A major focus of this role is serving as the primary programmatic and operational liaison between DAAS leadership, internal Enterprise IT Project Managers, and external vendor development teams to ensure division business, statutory, and workflow requirements are met throughout a multi-year IT systems replacement project.
Utilizing Lean thinking and continuous improvement principles (such as Arizona Management System / AMS practices), the Project Manager analyzes existing operational workflows, identifies process waste, and implements data-driven solutions to optimize program delivery for Arizona's aging and vulnerable adult populations. This position facilitates cross-functional collaboration, champions organizational change management, develops and tracks key performance metrics, and ensures strategic alignment across all divisional initiatives.

2. Major Responsibilities

40% – IT Systems Replacement Coordination & Implementation: Serves as the primary operational liaison between DAAS program units, internal Enterprise IT, and external vendor development teams to ensure division business requirements and regulatory standards are met throughout the systems replacement lifecycle. Coordinates cross-functional workgroups, tracks milestone deliverables, and oversees User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and operational readiness.
25% – Implementation of Continuous Improvement Initiatives: Manages implementation plans for divisional continuous improvement projects utilizing Lean thinking and Arizona Management System (AMS) principles to support operational efficiency and waste reduction. Tracks and coordinates the rollout of countermeasures—such as revised workflows, standard work, or visual management tools—and monitors key performance indicators to ensure sustainability. 15% – Strategic Project Execution & Divisional Alignment: Partners with the Strategy Manager to plan, lead, and deliver high-priority strategic initiatives that support the division's multi-year goals. Defines project scope, monitors milestones, and prepares executive-level briefings to ensure strategic alignment across all programs.
15% – Stakeholder Communication & Executive Reporting: Develops and maintains structured communication channels and reporting mechanisms to keep DAAS leadership and key stakeholders informed of project health, milestones, and risks. Prepares executive status presentations and performance briefings to drive transparency and data-informed decision-making.
5% – Other Duties as Assigned: Performs other duties as assigned related to the position to support emerging division priorities, special assignments, and operational needs.

3. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)

Knowledge of:

Formal project management principles, methodologies, and frameworks across multiple disciplines, including Predictive (Waterfall) and Adaptive (Agile/Scrum/Kanban) delivery models.
Lean and Six Sigma principles, continuous improvement tools, and operational management systems (e.g., Arizona Management System / AMS, DMAIC framework, 5S, visual management boards, countermeasure deployment).
Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) phases, including business requirements gathering, workflow mapping, gap analysis, and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) coordination.
Strategic planning frameworks, Key Performance Indicator (KPI) development, and performance measurement methodologies.
Principles and techniques of vendor coordination, contractual deliverable tracking, and milestone monitoring.
State and federal administrative guidelines, data privacy standards, and public agency operations (knowledge of human services, aging programs, or adult protective services is advantageous).

Skill in:

Applying both Waterfall (Gantt charts, critical paths, milestone schedules) and Agile (sprint tracking, backlogs, user stories) project management tools and techniques.
Managing project management software platforms and collaboration tools (e.g., Jira, Trello, Azure DevOps, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Monday.com, Visio, Lucid, SharePoint).
Developing clear, concise executive briefings, dashboards, status reports, and presentations tailored to diverse audiences.
Facilitating productive cross-functional workgroups, requirement-vetting sessions, and stakeholder meetings.
Identifying, analyzing, and documenting operational bottlenecks, project dependencies, and programmatic risks.
Tracking, prioritizing, and managing implementation tasks and countermeasure schedules across multiple concurrent initiatives.

Ability to:

Effectively bridge communication and translate concepts between non-technical program staff, internal enterprise IT professionals, and external third-party software developers.
Organize, prioritize, and drive multiple high-stakes projects simultaneously under evolving operational priorities and deadlines.
Build trust, consensus, and productive working relationships across varied organizational levels, external vendors, and community partners.
Maintain objectivity, analyze quantitative/qualitative data, and make sound, evidence-based recommendations to leadership.
Work independently with minimal supervision while maintaining strong strategic alignment with the Strategy Manager and executive priorities.
Champion continuous improvement and adapt readily to shifting technological environments and organizational needs.

4. Required Education, Licensure, and Certification

High School Diploma or General Educational Development (GED) equivalent.
Active Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) credential (or equivalent entry/associate-level project management certification from a reputable, accredited entity such as the Project Management Institute [PMI]).
Valid Arizona Driver License (with an acceptable driving record, if occasional in-state travel is required).

5. Preferred Education, Licensure, and Certification

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Business Administration, Public Administration, Information Technology, Project Management, Healthcare Administration, or a closely related field.
Active Project Management Professional (PMP) credential from the Project Management Institute (PMI).
Lean or Six Sigma certification (e.g., Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Yellow Belt, or formal Arizona Management System / AMS certification).
Agile or Scrum credentials (e.g., PMI-Agile Certified Practitioner [PMI-ACP], Certified ScrumMaster [CSM]

NO C2C!!!! W2 ONLY!!!! GC or USC!!!

Role Overview
Intuit is seeking a technically strong Data Analyst to support risk analytics, model implementation, loss forecasting and dashboard development across financial technology products.
The position will initially focus on payroll-related risk and loss forecasting
, with the potential to expand into other Intuit products involving lending, payments and money movement.
The team currently has some existing analytical capabilities but wants to expand its ability to forecast losses, implement models and develop dashboards that support financial risk decisions.
Important:
This is not a traditional reporting-only Data Analyst position. The hiring manager wants someone who combines advanced SQL, strong Python, data visualization and quantitative problem-solving with an understanding of financial risk.
Candidates do not need to be experienced model developers if they are technically strong and capable of learning.
Team & Business Context
The team evaluates financial exposure associated with Intuit's financial products.
Examples include:
Lending Risk:
Estimating potential losses when customers default on loans.
Payments / Money Movement Risk:
Evaluating losses associated with moving funds between merchants or customers.
Payroll Risk:
Building additional risk monitoring, modeling and loss forecasting capabilities for payroll-related products.

The team uses models to estimate future losses and determine the appropriate financial reserves.
The new hire will initially support payroll, but the role is intended to have cross-product applications.
Primary Business Objectives
Improve the team's ability to forecast financial losses.
Implement and support risk models.
Build dashboards to monitor financial exposure.
Investigate unexpected trends or changes in risk metrics.
Improve the availability and accuracy of analytical data.
Support business decisions through quantitative analysis.
Expand risk analytics capabilities across additional financial products.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities
SQL & Python Development
Write complex SQL queries to extract, transform and analyze large datasets.
Use Python to perform data analysis and support modeling workflows.
Develop analytical pipelines to support risk reporting and forecasting.
Review and validate code generated using AI tools.
Ensure calculations, metric definitions and outputs are accurate.
Investigate discrepancies in data and reporting.

Risk Modeling & Loss Forecasting
Support implementation of financial risk and loss forecasting models.
Analyze historical loss patterns and financial exposure.
Evaluate how lending or payment-related decisions affect potential losses.
Support forecasting of future losses.
Develop hypotheses to explain changes in risk metrics.
Investigate whether model outputs align with expected business outcomes.
Work with stakeholders to understand risk policies and business requirements.

Dashboarding & Reporting
Build dashboards to monitor risk performance and forecasted losses.
Create visualizations that make complex financial data understandable.
Track important KPIs and financial risk metrics.
Develop dashboards using Amazon QuickSight or comparable tools.
Support dashboard development through GitHub and AI-assisted workflows.
Ensure reported metrics accurately reflect business definitions.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
Work directly with business partners to gather requirements.
Proactively identify stakeholders who can provide needed information.
Clarify business questions before beginning development.
Translate business requirements into analytical solutions.
Communicate findings and recommendations.
Independently investigate issues and propose solutions.

The manager emphasized that candidates should not simply begin coding when they receive a request. They must first understand the business objective, confirm metric definitions and ensure the solution addresses the correct problem.
Top Technical Skills
1. Advanced SQL – Critical
Candidates should demonstrate strong SQL expertise, including:
Complex querying.
Large-scale data analysis.
Data manipulation and transformation.
Data validation.
Analytical calculations.
Developing datasets for reporting and forecasting.

The hiring manager expects a high level of SQL proficiency.
2. Python – Critical
Python is a significant requirement, not simply a nice-to-have.
The call clarified that SQL and Python are approximately equally important, with a 50/50 weighting
.
Candidates should be comfortable using Python for:
Data analysis.
Quantitative calculations.
Model implementation support.
Data pipeline development.
Reviewing AI-generated code.
Investigating data quality or forecasting issues.

3. Amazon QuickSight – Preferred
QuickSight was identified as the preferred dashboarding technology.
Candidates should have experience:
Creating dashboards.
Visualizing business metrics.
Developing analytical reporting.
Presenting complex data in a usable format.

The manager also mentioned dashboards developed through GitHub and LLM-assisted workflows.
QuickSight is highly desirable, but the discussion characterized it as a good-to-have rather than an absolute requirement.

Additional Technical Skills
AI / LLM Tools
The team wants someone comfortable leveraging LLMs to improve analytical workflows.
Relevant capabilities include:
Using LLMs to generate code.
Building or accelerating data pipelines.
Creating dashboards with AI assistance.
Reviewing AI-generated code for correctness.
Validating metrics and business definitions.

The manager does not want candidates who blindly accept AI-generated outputs.
They must understand the underlying logic and verify that the results are accurate.
Large-Scale Data Systems
Experience with large-scale MPP (massively parallel processing) database systems is highly desirable.
The manager indicated that much of the team's data will flow into Databricks
.
MPP experience is a strong plus.
Experience working with large-scale datasets is valuable.
Databricks familiarity is beneficial.
Direct MPP experience is not a dealbreaker.

Quantitative Analysis
Candidates should have experience with:
Quantitative problem-solving.
Forecasting.
Hypothesis development.
Statistical or analytical reasoning.
Explaining changes in metrics.
Validating analytical results.

Previous experience building sophisticated forecasting models is beneficial, but the manager is willing to train someone who has strong technical fundamentals.
Domain Experience
Preferred: Financial Technology Risk

Relevant backgrounds include:
Credit risk.
Lending risk.
Payment risk.
Money movement risk.
Financial loss forecasting.
Financial exposure analysis.
Risk analytics supporting FinTech products.

Relevant Industry Backgrounds
FinTech.
Banking.
Lending.
Payments.
Financial services.
Mortgage or credit-related risk functions.

The strongest candidates will combine technical analytical skills with experience assessing financial losses or financial exposure.
Domain knowledge is important, but the manager ranked it behind technical ability and independent problem-solving.

Risk Experience Clarification
The manager described risk primarily in terms of potential financial losses.
For example, if a lending decision results in a customer defaulting on a loan, Intuit may incur a financial loss. The team needs to forecast that exposure.
Similarly, moving payments between merchants can create financial exposure that must be evaluated.
This is different from a role focused primarily on cybersecurity or payment security monitoring.
Top 3 Hiring Priorities

The manager wants someone who can:
Independently engage business stakeholders.
Gather and clarify requirements.
Ask thoughtful questions.
Proactively obtain missing information.
Understand the business problem before developing a solution.
Work with minimal day-to-day supervision.

Advanced SQL.
Strong Python.
Ability to develop analytical solutions.
Comfort using LLMs to assist with coding.
Ability to validate code, calculations and business metrics.
Dashboarding and data analysis experience.

Preferred experience includes:
FinTech risk.
Credit risk.
Lending.
Payments.
Money movement.
Financial loss forecasting.

Position Summary

The Business Analyst, Planning & Analytics plays a critical role in helping Arva scale efficiently and sustainably. This role is responsible for forecasting and optimizing organizational capacity across our lines of business, ensuring that our teams, resources, and supported acres remain aligned with business demand and delivery commitments.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Portfolio Management, the Business Analyst will be a key contributor to workforce planning, acreage allocation, portfolio forecasting, and operational planning. This individual will analyze complex operational and business data to identify trends, anticipate constraints, and provide leaders with clear, actionable insights to support better planning and decision-making.

The ideal candidate brings a strong analytical foundation, experience working in operational or business planning environments, and the ability to translate complex data into straightforward, business-focused recommendations. They are comfortable working across functions, navigating ambiguity, and balancing analytical rigor with practical execution.

Capacity Planning & Forecasting

Build and maintain workforce capacity models across lines of business, including Customer Success capacity tied to acres under management.
Forecast resource demand, utilization, and staffing needs using sales pipelines, customer commitments, operational workloads, and strategic initiatives.
Identify capacity triggers, bottlenecks, and resource constraints before they affect delivery.
Create scenario analyses to support hiring and workforce planning decisions.
Provide analysis and options to support acreage allocation and resource reallocation decisions.

Portfolio Analytics & Reporting

Gather, clean, and analyze data from multiple sources to produce accurate portfolio and workforce insights.
Build and maintain dashboards, reports, and scorecards that show capacity, utilization, workload, and operational performance.
Track leading indicators and key metrics that support proactive portfolio management.
Deliver timely analyses and recommendations to support data-driven decisions.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Work closely with Customer Success, Sales, Operations, Product, and other teams to understand current and future workload drivers.
Translate pipeline forecasts, customer commitments, and business opportunities into capacity requirements.
Support discussions on resource prioritization, tradeoffs, and operational readiness.
Surface opportunities to improve efficiency and productivity through process or resource changes.

Process Improvement & Operational Excellence

Support the Senior Director of Portfolio Management in refining portfolio management processes, governance, and operating procedures.
Help document and maintain standardized methodologies for forecasting, capacity planning, and resource management.
Contribute to evaluating and adopting tools, reporting structures, and workflows that improve visibility and planning accuracy.
Participate in continuous improvement initiatives focused on scalability, predictability, and execution.

Communication

Prepare clear, concise presentations, reports, and recommendations for leadership review.
Turn complex datasets and analyses into simple, actionable insights.
Present findings and forecasts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Analytics, Economics, or a related field.
3–8 years of experience in capacity planning, workforce planning, operations, portfolio management, business analytics, sales operations, or a related discipline.
Experience building forecasts, resource models, or operational planning tools.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and/or Google Sheets, including complex formulas, data modeling, pivot tables, scenario analysis, and large dataset management.
Strong experience gathering, organizing, and analyzing data from multiple sources.
Ability to independently obtain, consolidate, and structure the data needed to support business decisions.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills with exceptional attention to detail.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in both sales and operational environments.
Proficiency with business intelligence and visualization tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or similar platforms.
Experience with portfolio, project, or resource management platforms.
Familiarity with forecasting methods, workforce planning models, and operational KPI development.
Experience supporting a high-growth organization through scaling and operational change.
Interest in agriculture, sustainability, or mission-driven work.

Critical Success Competencies

Analytical Mindset:
Evaluates complex datasets, identifies patterns, and turns findings into actionable recommendations.
Workforce Planning Awareness:
Understands how sales pipelines, customer demand, and operational workloads affect future resource needs.
Business Acumen:
Balances operational realities with growth objectives when analyzing capacity and resource needs.
Data Storytelling:
Communicates analyses and recommendations simply, concisely, and persuasively.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Builds strong working relationships across departments and helps drive alignment on capacity planning and priorities.
Continuous Improvement:
Looks for ways to improve processes, increase efficiency, and strengthen execution.
Deliver dashboards that give clear visibility into resource demand, utilization, and capacity risks.
Support proactive staffing decisions through data-driven forecasting.
Improve forecast accuracy and reduce surprises related to workload and capacity.
Identify and help implement process improvements that increase operational efficiency.
Become a trusted analytical partner to leadership and cross-functional teams.

Why Join Arva

This is a chance to apply strong analytical skills to work that matters. You will help shape how a fast-growing company scales its impact, supporting the growers, partners, and customers who are making agriculture more resilient and sustainable.

Employment Eligibility

Only applicants currently, and in the future, eligible to work in the United States will be considered for this position.

About Arva

Arva is a machine learning software-based SaaS company with offices located in Houston, TX and Park City, UT. Arva's platform was built to apply our novel ML technology to the agricultural industry, optimizing and measuring regenerative practices, improving crop yields, and reducing operational costs for producers. Our platform helps our customers and partners capitalize on "natural regenerative practices" by providing recommendations that improve environmental and ecological ecosystems. Platform features include practice verification and registration, as well as the sale of environmental asset credits to our corporate buyers. Thus, Arva is helping to keep the planet green by providing a "green-tech" platform that informs, measures, validates, and registers carbon exchange opportunities, allowing growers and ranchers to produce and sell credits that are bought by our corporate partners, who endorse sustainable food supply and carbon neutrality.

As Arva scales its work with global enterprise CPG partners, we are seeking an experienced Global Client Partner to own end-to-end client delivery, cross-functional coordination, and relationship depth across Arva's largest global accounts.

Arva exists to scale regenerative agriculture. We connect farmers and corporations through technology that measures what’s happening on the land, enabling growers to be rewarded for improving soil health while helping businesses achieve their sustainability goals with measurable, verified results. As our programs and impact continue to grow, thoughtful capacity planning and resource allocation are critical to ensuring we can scale effectively while maintaining the quality of our work.

This job description reflects the core duties of the role but is not intended to be all-inclusive. The role may evolve as the company grows, requiring additional responsibilities or changes in scope.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Policy & Intergovernmental Affairs
jobs.description:
Job Summary

This position is open until filled; however, to ensure consideration applications should be received by December 7, 2026 at 4:30 p.m.

KCHA is currently recruiting for a talented Senior Program Manager to join the Policy and Intergovernmental Affairs team located in Tukwila, Washington.

The Senior Program Manager, Policy & Intergovernmental Affairs is a strategic leadership role responsible for advancing KCHA’s mission through policy development, program innovation, and intergovernmental partnerships. This position leads analysis and implementation of federal housing policies under the Moving to Work (MTW) program, collaborates across the agency to develop and evaluate impactful programs, and ensures compliance with HUD requirements. The role also builds relationships with peer agencies and key stakeholders, while leading the development of reports, policy analyses, and communications that inform decision-making and demonstrate KCHA’s impact. Reporting to the Vice President of Policy & Intergovernmental Affairs, this position is ideal for a collaborative leader passionate about housing policy and community impact.

King County Housing Authority (KCHA) is the largest provider of affordable housing in the Pacific Northwest and a nationally recognized leader in affordable housing. To learn more about KCHA and our Mission visit this link .

Essential Functions

Tracks, monitors, researches, and reports on complex legislation at the federal, state, and local levels in a fast-paced environment and prepares policy and advocacy materials related to affordable housing.
Develops, writes, and edits communications on complex topics for external audiences.
Participates in and represents KCHA at meetings with local, state, and national coalitions and alliances of other affordable housing providers and advocacy groups.
Manages and ensures Agency compliance with federal regulations under the Moving to Work (MTW) program; tracks MTW-related issues, reviews notices and proposed rules and analyzes impacts on the Agency, and drafts comments and coordinates with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for clarification when necessary.
Writes and manages development of the Agency’s MTW Plan and Report and its submission to HUD; leads the community engagement process for MTW; oversees MTW activities for compliance; ensures that the agency meets the MTW planning and reporting requirements and associated deadlines.
Coordinates, facilitates meetings, and works with multiple individuals and departments to ensure smooth, coherent, accurate, timely, and high-quality planning and reporting requirements are met.
Leads strategic efforts with Agency leadership to evaluate and establish new policies and programs within the development of an annual agency-wide MTW Plan; implements processes to synthesize plans and progress by other departments; discusses policy development and provides guidance for department leaders.
Conceptualizes, develops, and executes policy initiatives for the Agency; develops and coordinates cross-sector, strategic partnerships with local, state, and national organizations and other housing authorities; provides project management for agency's work in developing long-term policy strategies.
Gathers and interprets housing and fiscal data and develops dashboards on high-level agency trends to inform the Board and Executive Team on ongoing operational outcomes and long-term utilization of the MTW Block Grant.
Prepares and delivers presentations to Board of Commissioners and executive leaders on complex policy and intergovernmental affairs.
Manages, plans and represents KCHA in events such as legislative briefings, community forums, and elected official visits.

Qualifications and Competencies

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree AND

Considerable experience in policy development and analysis, project management, intergovernmental affairs, and regulatory reporting OR

An equivalent combination of experience and education that provides the necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Understands technical aspects of the position and continuously builds knowledge, keeping up-to-date on the substantive and procedural aspects of the position.
Thorough knowledge, understanding, and ability to interpret federal, state and local regulations, policies, and procedures related to affordable housing, U.S. Department of Housing and Development (HUD), and applicable federal, state, and local laws, and regulations, policies, and research regarding Moving to Work (MTW) projects, practices, and programs.
Extensive experience in policy development, legislative analysis, program evaluation, and strategic planning within affordable housing, public policy, or a related field.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex data, assess policy impacts, and develop actionable recommendations for senior leadership.
Demonstrated ability to lead high-priority initiatives, manage multiple complex projects, and drive results in a dynamic environment.
Applies effective written and verbal communication techniques to convey clear and timely messages to internal and external stakeholders; communicates clearly and effectively via multiple methods.
Demonstrated experience preparing executive-level reports, presentations, policy briefs, and stakeholder communications.
Presents proposals and recommendations clearly, logically and persuasively; prepares clear and concise reports.
Values diversity and possesses an understanding of multicultural and cultural competencies; ability to work effectively and positively with individuals of diverse cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds.
Effective interpersonal skills with the ability to work collaboratively to garner the trust, respect, and confidence from others; can be relied upon to achieve excellent results; ability to work effectively under pressure in a fast paced environment.
Ability to influence decision-making and provide strategic guidance on legislative, regulatory, and organizational issues.
Demonstrated leadership skills, including the ability to mentor, collaborate across departments, and represent the organization in high-level public and professional settings.
Proven experience building and maintaining effective partnerships with government agencies, elected officials, community organizations, industry partners, and executive stakeholders.
Proficiency in data analysis and reporting tools, including Microsoft Office Suite, with advanced Excel skills preferred.
Strong judgment, political acumen, and the ability to navigate sensitive issues while balancing competing priorities and interests.

Special Requirements:

Final candidates may be required to complete a driver's and criminal background check in accordance with applicable law.
Must possess a valid driver's license and own or have access to a vehicle to regularly travel between work sites or have an alternative reliable mode of transportation.

Position Information and Application Process

Application Requirements:

jobs.description:
Senior Data Analyst - Strategy

Remote | Analytics & Strategy

$120,000-$140,000

Overview

An organization working across complex public-sector and social-impact challenges is seeking a Senior Data Analyst to support strategic decision-making through rigorous data analysis.
This person will act as a cross-functional problem solver, working with senior stakeholders to address broad, often ambiguous questions. They will identify and combine relevant public and internal datasets, assess what the available information can reliably tell us, and translate their findings into clear recommendations and actionable insights.
The role is particularly suited to someone with strong statistical skills, experience working with complex public or administrative datasets, and the ability to exercise independent judgment when working with incomplete or imperfect information.

Key Responsibilities

Work across multiple subject areas to investigate complex questions and support strategic decision-making.

Identify, source, and combine publicly available and internal datasets to answer business and policy-related questions.

Apply statistical methods to analyze imperfect, incomplete, and complex datasets.

Develop reproducible analytical models and well-documented code.

Translate analytical findings into clear reports, decision memos, and recommendations for senior stakeholders.

Independently assess data quality, limitations, and the extent to which findings can support particular conclusions.

Required Qualifications

3-5+ years of applied analytics experience, ideally within a strategy consulting, analytics consulting, economic consulting, or similarly demanding environment.

Candidates with experience leading analytics work within a high-growth organization or public-sector agency will also be considered.

Strong quantitative academic background, including a STEM discipline or applied quantitative social science such as Economics, Statistics, Urban Studies, Operations Research, or Population Health.

Professional experience coding in Python or SQL, including building analytical workflows and querying datasets.

Experience producing reproducible, well-documented code.

Hands-on experience working with complex public-sector, administrative, or publicly available datasets.

Strong understanding of statistical methods, including regression, sampling and weighting, hypothesis testing, missing data, and statistical uncertainty.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with program evaluation, quasi-experimental research, or causal inference.

Background in social-impact areas such as housing, public health, community safety, or related policy areas.

Familiarity with geographic or spatial analysis.

Experience working in government, nonprofit, consulting, or policy-focused environments.

Familiarity with AI-assisted research and analytical workflows, including LLM-assisted coding, prompt engineering, thematic analysis, and output validation.

Demonstrated academic or professional excellence, such as a strong educational background, experience at a selective consultancy, rapid career progression, or ownership of particularly challenging analytical projects.
